description: Provenance check of the driving docs (00, 07, 08, 10-13) on 2026-10-10: each claim's value found in a research-workspace result (by experiment ID) or recomputed from bundled data. 'corrected' rows were rewritten in the docs to the value given here; 'unsupported' rows were removed from the docs or replaced with sourced numbers.

claims.claim: excursions ramp up over ~1.5 s and decay over ~2 s
claims.source: research workspace SCR-115; earlier repo text only
claims.note: Contradicting retained wording: SCR-417 (data/derived/ars510_excursion_cause_20261003/result.md) 'ensemble onset/end shapes (25 events) ramp over ~1 s'; docs/07 waveform section itself says 'build up over 1-2 s'. Suggest '~1-2 s'.

claims.claim: ~0.1 per 1,000 records below 20 m, 130 at 60-80 m
claims.source: research workspace SCR-115; bundled signal_atlas_and_acc_crosscheck.json; earlier repo text only
claims.note: Discovery-half numbers not retained; confirmation gives ~10 and ~223 per 1000 (rate denominator not recorded; script not retained, likely clean-labelled ACC+vision-matched records, not all records). Only the ratio (31x / 22x) and false-closing share 0.84 / 0.875 are in JSON.

claims.claim: ~18% of track time at 100 m
claims.note: Different label than the per-1000 rates in the same sentence (SCR-129 double-witness drift samples: range-closure residual and vision); sample share, i.e. ~track time.

claims.claim: gap to ACC ramps from about -1 to -3.4 m/s
claims.source: research workspace SCR-115; earlier repo text only
claims.note: No retained number or script; clean_labels.py/mech.py outputs lack it.

claims.claim: 1.7% of record-to-record steps exceed 2 m/s
claims.source: research workspace SCR-115; earlier repo text only
claims.note: Not recomputable from public data (needs ACC target + vision labels).

claims.claim: range confirms a drift after 2-4 s
claims.note: An inference (a 2-3 m/s drift needs ~2-4 s to exceed the walk), not a measured onset delay. Wording 'range alone confirms ... only after 2-4 s' was in older text.

claims.claim: error is low-pass (~0.3 Hz)
1.4 m/s at code 30 (0.8 at code 15)
claims.note: 0.8 at code 15 is the measured RMS; 1.4 at 30 is the K=0.045 model. Measured at code 30 is ~1.2 m/s. Use '1.2 m/s at code 30' or say both are K x code.

claims.claim: on a highway about 5 slots hold objects
claims.note: 'about 5' matches neither mean nor p95; suggest 'about 2 (up to 7)'.

claims.claim: roughness +0.005 (steady following) / +0.032 (switch windows) m/s^2 RMS; switch windows 20% of time
claims.source: research workspace SCR-119; bundled jitter_problem_figures.json, jitter_source_and_interface_limit.json

claims.claim: about 70% of the extra roughness
yvRel yaw rate (Toyota 0x24) matches phone gyro at 1.02x
claims.note: Possible conflict: <path> says CAN 0x24 yaw is ~3-5% high vs device gyro (cites an older findings.md line no longer present). Not recomputable from public data (no yaw).

claims.claim: yvRel follows d(yRel)/dt at r = 0.88, slope 0.86
claims.note: No workspace record; not recomputable (no yaw in public data).

claims.claim: aRel lags vRel by 0.5-1 s
claims.note: Only weakly coupled (r~0.22) with a broad peak 0.3-0.9 s; original claim from commit 5159253 had no saved source.

claims.claim: 17.5% of radard ticks repeat the previous vRel; adds ~1% to aLeadK roughness
StarPilot 2 drives / 18 min
claims.note: 18 min = openpilot-longitudinal time (17.7 min); drives were ~45 min in total. Current doc line only says '(2 drives)'.

claims.claim: sunnypilot 2 drives with the earlier profile
claims.note: Old default profile, ARS510 active (flags 5465); route 2 drove vision-only, route 5 parked. The 09-28 first drives (ars510_sunnypilot_drive_check_20260928) ran without the radar.

claims.claim: StarPilot extrapolates lead acceleration unchanged above 35 mph
about 9 us per call
claims.note: Order of magnitude holds; samples carry only bus-1 radar + 0xB4 frames, so real calls with all bus-0 traffic cost a bit more. Suggest '~6-15 us per 10 ms call'.

claims.claim: check_integration passes 21-22 checks
claims.note: Sunnypilot counts are from 2026-09-28/30 builds; the 2026-10-04 release check could not complete sunnypilot (sparse source snapshot).

claims.claim: range fusion halves 1.5 s range walks
claims.note: Only source: first-commit (cee331d) summary 'opt-in fusion halves them ... H1 failed beyond 80 m on B'. Recompute: about one third less (x0.67-0.78), less beyond 80 m. fused uses filtered vRel, which may do better; not testable with public data. Suggest 'cuts 1.5 s range walks by about a third'.

claims.claim: aLeadK cascade lag 0 ticks on 14 of 15 routes, 1 tick on one
saturation guard: held-out hard ticks 117 -> 93
claims.note: velocity_guards.json is no longer in the public repo; 93 also appears as raw's hard ticks in profiles_vs_vision.json. Add the summary back or cite it in fused_filter.json.

claims.claim: 23 bookmarks give the same requests for 2.3 and 2.4 (SCR-494)
claims.note: Bookmarks: sn-17 11, sn-20 6, sn-1f 5, sn-18 1. Four minima differ by 0.01-0.03 m/s^2 (sn-17 4:09.8, 9:38.3, 101:00.0; sn-1f 78:08.1); 'same requests' holds to 0.03 m/s^2.

claims.claim: road mild requests 2.3 vs 2.4: 7 each
claims.note: Episode lists are identical: sn-17 1, sn-1b 1, sn-1d 1, sn-1f 1, sn-20 3 (owner = 7) plus ot-c3 1 (second car) = 8. lead_choice_guards road_drives_replay.owner '2.3 fused' mild 7 = owner only; cases_2_4 '8 mild across owner and second car'. Both consistent.

claims.claim: Kalman bench on 8 drive groups
claims.note: Tuned on 3 groups, scored on held-out / fresh / owner (public kalman_variants.json bench_definition).

claims.claim: retuned fused constants are as good as any on 8 fresh drives
claims.note: Sweep sigma/code 0.033, ACC sigma 0.3, lead accel 1.0/2.0: only lead accel 2.0 passes every gate and is not better; current constants at a flat optimum.

claims.claim: colored filter 15% fewer false closings
claims.note: 14-16% on held-out and fresh drives, 0% on owner drives; say 'on held-out and fresh drives'.

claims.claim: colored: 2 -> 30 hard ticks on the further drives
age 40: further-drive hard ticks 1 -> 9
claims.note: Baseline is 2.3 (CL_P15S).

claims.claim: age 80: missed braking vs oracle 3.0 -> 3.7 s on 27 drives
claims.note: Baseline 3.0 = 2.4 (corrected oracle). A80 was built on 2.3's config, whose corrected value is 3.3, so like-for-like it is 3.3 -> 3.7. SCR-492's original numbers (3.8 -> 4.3) predate the oracle fix.

claims.claim: Toyota ACC releases a departing car at |y| median 1.64 m (IQR 0.67-2.16, 22 departures)
0.29 m inside the radar's lane line (21 departures)
claims.note: IQR is wide (-1.26 to +0.42 m).

claims.claim: openpilot's model moved first, 1.5 s and > 6 s (n = 3)
claims.note: Source says '>= 6 s' and only 2 of the 3 cut-in-like ACC switches (1.9 h, fresh routes 08/09/0a) were matched; these were cut-ins, not departures. Source calls it inconclusive.

claims.claim: 0x235 byte 2 vs radard aLeadK: corr 0.64 vs 0.56, RMS 0.68 vs 0.80, ~0.35 s earlier
claims.note: The numbers come from SCR-424, not acc_target_arel.json. At the current 0.125: corr 0.64, RMS 0.69 vs 0.80 (barely changes) but the best-lag shift becomes 0.0 s, so 'about 0.35 s earlier' is fragile (0.36 s at 0.1, 0.84 s at 0.125). acc_target_arel.json (SCR-129) also decodes at 0.1: its binned medians should be x1.25; correlations unaffected, it has no RMS.

claims.claim: upstream file equal to fused point for point; two full drives checked once
claims.note: The 2-drive check was for 2.1.0; for 2.4 only the bundled-sample test (tests/test_upstream_candidate.py) covers equality. Note findings.md uses SCR-476 for two different rows (also ars510_slim_norange_20261005).

claims.claim: Ford radar_interface 268 lines, 194 code lines
claims.note: 194 matches neither checkout (195 = non-blank non-comment incl. docstrings on 6123dde9). Use 184 (272 lines) to match the table's other rows, or 180 (268) for current opendbc.

claims.claim: Tesla radar_interface 66 code lines
claims.note: Table rows (Toyota 70, Honda 60, Hyundai 55, Rivian 54, Chrysler 56, GM 71) all match 6123dde9; current opendbc has Tesla 62, Toyota 69.

claims.claim: 0x680 idle while driving: longest 1.0 s in 7.8 h
claims.note: 7.8 h = 7.25 + 0.55 moving hours; held-out longest 0.5 s.

claims.claim: missed hard slowdown window [-3, +1] s; anticipation [-3, +0.5]; first request [-3, +2]
claims.note: Table rows 'within 3 s before' (docs 08:147, 11:69-70) and profiles_vs_vision.json description ('within 3 s before the brake press') are shorthand; the window runs to +0.5 s.

claims.claim: Fewer than 10 events separate several rows
claims.note: Every event-count row differs by at most 7 events between columns; 'several' understates it.

claims.claim: 0x4FF ~0.77 Hz
claims.note: census prints 0.8 because it rounds to one decimal.

claims.claim: 0x411 over 773 owner segments (JSON counts 752 + 27 = 779)
claims.note: 752 and 27 overlap (the 27 also carry 00 20), so 779 is not a count. The payload census covers 752 segments; 773 is the event/alert scan. JSON key 'payloads_773_segments' should be 752 or the text should say 752.

claims.claim: 0x366 coverage drives A / B
claims.note: Relabel A/B as O2/O3 to match the 0x365 table in the same doc.
